summary: A solid edge-first Anycast DDoS architecture that keeps the hot path fully local to PoPs and uses a centralized control plane for bounded telemetry, anomaly detection, and short-lived mitigations with safe rollout/rollback. The design is broadly production-plausible and covers key L3/L4 and L7 attack classes, with pragmatic simplifications around telemetry and analytics.
strengths: Clear separation of fast-path edge enforcement from control-plane feedback, with last-known-good config, monotonic versioning, TTL mitigations, and rollback guardrails
Good practical details on resource budgeting (PPS/CPS/RPS caps, HTTP/2 Rapid Reset protections, progressive challenges) and bounded telemetry/top-K heavy hitters to stay operable under attack
weaknesses: Anycast/BGP and upstream mitigation operations are only sketched (routing health, congestion/overload handling, provider coordination, RTBH/FlowSpec safety, multi-transit failure modes)

Control-plane and data-store resiliency/scaling are under-specified for the stated targets (multi-region active-active, Postgres write/read hot spots, key management/HSM, config stream durability/backpressure)
